## Summary

Add SGR mouse-tracking enable/disable sequences tied to the TUI lifecycle (raw-mode entry / cleanup) and implement the pure SGR mouse-event parser. First implementation slice for WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ; covered by the test-first suite in WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ANSI constants added for mouse enable (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h`) and disable (`\x1b[?1000l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1006l`) in the existing `ANSI` object (worklist.ts ~line 133) (parent AC1)
- [ ] Enable sequences are written to stdout when the TUI enters raw mode; disable sequences are written in `cleanup()` (parent AC1) — verified by the test suite and a manual smoke-run
- [ ] Pure `parseMouseEvent(key: string)` recognizes `\x1b[<b;x;yM` (press) and `\x1b[<b;x;y m` (release) and returns `{ button, x, y, release } | null` (parent AC1, AC6)
- [ ] Partial sequences split across stdin chunks are buffered until the terminating M/m; non-mouse or unknown sequences return null without corrupting the keypress path (parent AC6 + risk mitigation)
- [ ] All tests from the test-first suite (WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC) that cover this slice pass; no existing `handleKeypress` tests regress (parent AC6)

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the `ANSI` object in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` with `mouseEnable` / `mouseDisable` entries
- Write enable sequences in the `runWorklistTui` raw-mode block and disable sequences in `cleanup()` (only when raw mode was entered)
- Add exported pure `parseMouseEvent` + a small module-level buffer for split chunks; document the SGR format in a comment

## Dependencies

- WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC (test suite defines expected behavior)

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` changes (ANSI constants, lifecycle emission, parser)
- Green tests for this slice
data.title: Implement: mouse tracking lifecycle + SGR parser

## Summary

Map parsed SGR mouse events to TUI actions — click/tap selects, double-click/tap opens details, wheel/touch scroll navigates, filter-prompt tap applies a stage — dispatched from onData before the keypress path. Core interaction slice for WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single left click/tap on a visible list row moves the selection to that item (equivalent of up/down arrow keys) (parent AC2)
- [ ] Double-click/tap within ~400 ms on the same row activates that item — the Enter-equivalent action for the current mode (list: open detail; detail: existing Enter semantics, mirrored as-is). Double-click state does not leak to unrelated rows (parent AC3)
- [ ] Wheel-up/wheel-down (buttons 64/65) and translated touch scrolls move the selection in list mode and scroll the detail content consistent with keyboard j/k (including the detail ToC-focus nuance from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I: wheel over the ToC moves ToC selection, wheel over the document scrolls it) (parent AC4)
- [ ] Tapping a stage option row in the filter prompt applies that stage filter (equivalent of the digit key) (parent AC5)
- [ ] Drag-motion events (button code with the 32 motion bit) never cause selection jumps; clicks on non-list areas (header, notification row, metadata panel) are ignored safely (parent constraints + risk mitigation)
- [ ] Mouse-shaped sequences are fully consumed before the keypress path; unknown/unparsable sequences are inert — no crash, no state corruption; all existing keyboard navigation and chord/shortcut behavior is unchanged; existing `handleKeypress` tests pass (parent AC6)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a pure row-mapping helper converting 1-based y to a list row (header offset + scrollOffset), a detail scroll position, or a filter option depending on `state.mode` — reuse geometry from `createListRenderer` (header row, listArea, panelHeight)
- Add `mapMouseToAction(state, mouseEvent, termSize)` returning a dispatchable action (select-row, open-detail, wheel-up/down, scroll-detail, filter-stage, etc.)
- Dispatch from `onData` before the keypress path; track last-click time/position for the ~400 ms double-click window

## Dependencies

- WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC (test suite)
- WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM (parser + lifecycle)

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` changes (row mapping, mouse dispatch, double-click tracking)
- Green tests for this slice, including unknown-sequence regression (parent AC6)

# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Document version display

## Summary
Update the Herdr plugin documentation to describe the dimmed, right-aligned plugin version shown in the work item selection list header.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `packages/herdr/README.md` documents that the work item selection list header shows the running plugin version (dimmed, right-aligned).
- Documentation is consistent with the implemented behaviour (F2), including the fallback when the version is unavailable.
- CHANGELOG.md is NOT modified (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a bullet under the Features section (and/or a short note in the relevant UI section) of `packages/herdr/README.md` describing the version display.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: implementation (F2) — document the implemented behaviour, not the intended one.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Summary

The shared test runner (skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py) defines a static NODE_SUITE_DIRS = (tests/node, tests/cli, tests/unit). ContextHub has no tests/node directory (git ls-files confirms it was never tracked), so the canonical full-suite command npm --silent test -- tests/node always exits 1 with 'No test files found'.

## Impact

The audit skill's automatic full-suite verification (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W) queries the per-repo test cache for EVERY canonical suite command and requires exit code 0. The permanently-failing tests/node entry means the audit runner can NEVER inject automatic green-run evidence for ContextHub audits — execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'Full project test suite passes') stay partial and block closure.

## Workaround used in release v1.0.9

Operator ran pytest (103 passed) + npx vitest run (4117 passed) at the release HEAD and passed --green-run HEAD to each audit — honest attestation, but manual.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) filter NODE_SUITE_DIRS by directory existence in the shared runner, or (b) make ContextHub's suite definition explicit. Discovered during release v1.0.9 remediation (discovered-from:WL-0MSG80FQ9000C8GE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The canonical full-suite command set for ContextHub (as resolved by full_suite_commands()) matches the suites that actually exist in the repo.
- [ ] run_tests.py --summary --suite all reports green for every suite in the canonical set at a green HEAD.
data.title: Audit auto-green-run never works for ContextHub: NODE_SUITE_DIRS includes tests/node which does not exist
